directive.thread_id: film repository port 2026-11-05, lane film-tools, sub-lane checks: the rendered-video checker's helper scripts
directive.quote: Finish the port of the film repository so it can be retired: move each job to its correct home, porting the correct parts one to one and never rebuilding from scratch what already worked; settings are rows in the person's lists, read through the door.

targets.baseline_commit_message: check-a-rendered-video: the film checker-owner's inspect and span-export scripts, moved byte for byte

preserve: needed: per spec, the source seconds its preview plays through ctx.source_time at every frame of edit.preview, one range per run of consecutive frames, padded
union and subtract of the ranges against the spans placement.bases already holds
nothing exported while a media file of the editor's project is offline (exit 2)
each export probed (frame size, rate, duration within a tolerance) and refused otherwise
exports run one at a time under the render lock, not waited on when the parent holds it
allowed_deltas: the specs folder, limits (a file or the person's list:settings row), bases key, frame rate, pad, tolerance, output folder, file name and lock are arguments; the film's folder, project and limits paths above the copied lines are gone
the exporter is the person's own command line (argv with {out}, {from}, {to}) instead of the film's editor call
the answer gives the rows to add to placement.bases instead of writing an edit file for the limits file
a range that rounds to nothing is not exported (the old script asked for two zero-length exports on its own round-8 specs)
banned_substitutions: a person's limits file path, film folder or name written in code
a second implementation of a check's numbers beside the check module itself
a fixed exporter, frame size or frame rate
_paths: A source in the private film repository is named by the BLAKE3 identity of its path (path_multihash); a checkout of that repository beside this one finds it.
